answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each agent identity an anchor to a cryptographically attested enclave measurement, MRENCLAVE, verified through a remote-attestation chain before participation. The verifier accepts only code and platform evidence matching the registered policy, so duplicating an identity in virtual machines cannot reproduce its trusted hardware key. An attacker must instead acquire physical silicon and a genuine enclave, while attempts to forge measurements or replay attestations are rejected; saffron is merely an application label, not an identity.
